Kisuke is a Kaminarimon washoku house whose two signatures are 京風おでん and charcoal 焼き鳥 from Iwate branded chicken, with a shorter jidori skewer list rotated by supply — the shop warns 「仕入れ、生産者の都合上全種類のご提供が出来ない場合が御座います」, so the six named jidori are not all available on any given night. Skewers are ordered one at a time, 塩 or タレ. ⚠ THE 塩/タレ CHOICE IS THE SINGLE MOST USEFUL FACT HERE FOR A COELIAC AND IT DOES NOT GET YOU ALL THE WAY: タレ is a soy-sauce glaze and therefore wheat, 塩 is salt — but both cook over the same charcoal and are handled with the same tongs, and the shop publishes no allergen statement and makes no separation claim, so every skewer is recorded ask rather than gf. ⚠ THE ODEN DASHI IS A DOUBLE FACT: the shop states it is drawn from 北海道日高昆布と鶏のガラ, Hidaka kombu AND CHICKEN BONES, which closes the entire oden pot to a vegan even for the vegetable pieces, and oden dashi is conventionally finished with usukuchi soy, which the shop does not address. ⚠ TWO ODEN PIECES ARE WHEAT UNDER JAPANESE NAMES THAT DO NOT LOOK LIKE IT: くるま麩 is pure wheat gluten (and, in itself, perfectly vegan — it is the broth that disqualifies it here), and ちくわぶ is NOT a fish cake despite the name, it is a wheat-flour dumpling; the fish-cake one is 鯛の焼きちくわ, which is surimi. ⚠ AND THE SOBA SECTION IS HONEST IN A WAY MOST ARE NOT: the shop labels its noodles 二八 and 十割 separately, so the 二八 is declared 20% wheat. The 十割 is 100% buckwheat, but 打ち粉 is wheat, the boiling water is shared with the 二八 and the tempura, and the dipping tsuyu is soy — so it is recorded no, with the ratio recorded because the honesty is worth having. Alcohol note: the two flat-rate drink packages are only sold to course bookings.

tokyo_kukurihime_coffee.price_note: Full card from the shop’s own お品書き page, all prices 税込. Kukurihime is an Asakusa self-roasting coffee house whose actual subject is 和パフェ — Japanese-Western parfaits — plus house nut butters. Drinks are priced twice, for drinking in and for takeaway, and takeaway is cheaper by 100yen on every line; both are recorded. Parfaits are priced 単品 or セット, the セット being the parfait with a drink, and where the shop prints only a セット price that is what is recorded. The shop notes スイーツセット drinks may be chosen from the drink list, with a +100yen supplement if the chosen drink is an 800yen one. ⚠ THE STRUCTURAL FACT FOR A COELIAC IS THE PARFAIT ITSELF: a Japanese parfait is a stack, and the crunchy layer at the bottom is where wheat hides. The shop names it outright on two items — the 盆栽 pair are built on サクサクのパイ生地, PASTRY, which is wheat — and everything called a ケーキ or a ロールケーキ is a wheat sponge. What is left that is not built on wheat is the かき氷 (羽衣), the ice creams, the coffee, and the nut butters. ⚠ AND ALMOST NOTHING HERE IS VEGAN: 生クリーム, ソフトクリーム, 練乳 (condensed milk), ホワイトチョコ, レアチーズ and バニラアイス appear across the sweets, and the lattes are milk. The plain coffees, the teas, the lemonade and the two sodas are the plant-only end of the card. No allergen statement is published. tokyo_nihon_ryori_ichie.price_note: Ichie is a Hongo kaiseki house taking ONE PARTY PER DAY by reservation only, so there is no à la carte — the whole menu is two omakase courses, both priced per person and tax-included on the shop’s own page, and both carry the caveat 「ご予算は、市況により変動する場合がございます」, the price moves with the market. The shop asks for bookings five days ahead so it can secure ingredients; four days to the day before is enquiry-only. The September 2026 献立例 is reproduced in the item notes because a kaiseki course IS its menu. ⚠ FOR A COELIAC A KAISEKI HOUSE IS THE HARDEST FORMAT IN JAPANESE COOKING TO CLEAR AND THIS ONE PUBLISHES ITS OWN EVIDENCE: 生醤油 appears three times in the September courses by name — in the 肝だれ, in the 甘鯛竜田揚 where the fish is washed in it, and in the 向付 alongside 吟醸醤油 — and 竜田揚げ is by definition a soy marinade under a starch coat. The shop’s house 胡麻豆腐 is sesame and kuzu starch, which is the one component named here that is structurally wheat-free. ⚠ FOR A VEGAN IT IS CLOSED OUTRIGHT: the September course opens with a chawanmushi built on 鴨脂 — DUCK FAT — and free-range egg, and runs through abalone, sashimi, karasumi, wagyu and dried river fish; the suppon course is turtle in every one of its ten courses. ⚠ AND THE ONE THING TO ASK ABOUT IS THE 土鍋炊飯: the shop offers more than ten choices of clay-pot rice as the meal course, and a takikomi rice is seasoned with soy — the plain-rice option is the one to request. No allergen statement is published. The shop publishes a full English version of the menu. Tabelog not consulted: Cf-Mitigated: challenge (403) to this egress since 2026-09-02.

items.note: Nine to eleven courses, finished with 土鍋炊飯 clay-pot rice, a 止椀 and pickles. tokyo_taishoken_maruichi_shibu.price_note: ⚠ THE SHOP’S OWN メニュー紹介 PAGE NAMES EVERY DISH AND PRICES NONE OF THEM — it is a photo-led introduction, not a price list, and the Shibuya branch page carries no prices either. Every item below is therefore recorded with no price. Taishoken Maruichi is a tsukemen and ramen specialist with branches at Shibuya, Shinjuku Tonan-guchi and Akabane; this record is the Shibuya branch and the menu page is the brand’s, covering all three. ⚠ NOTHING IN THE NOODLE SECTIONS IS EVEN CLOSE TO GLUTEN-FREE AND THE SHOP TELLS YOU WHY WITHOUT MEANING TO: it advertises 自家製麺 made 材料から製法まで職人の手で — house-made noodles from the raw material up — and Japanese ramen and tsukemen noodles are wheat flour with kansui. The broth is 豚骨、鶏ガラ、野菜、煮干し simmered long, which is pork, chicken and dried sardine, so it fails vegan on three counts before the tare is added. The gyoza are wrapped in wheat. ⚠ THE ONLY ITEMS ON THIS CARD THAT ARE NOT STRUCTURALLY WHEAT ARE THE RICE, THE PLAIN TOPPINGS AND THE DRINKS — and 味玉 and メンマ are both marinated, conventionally in soy. Seasonal limited items run alongside. No allergen statement is published. Tabelog not consulted: Cf-Mitigated: challenge (403) to this egress since 2026-09-02.

The noodle is offered in two cuts, 中太縮れ麺 or 低加水細麺, and both are wheat with kansui; the choice is texture, not diet. No allergen statement is published. tokyo_hakata_kushiyaki_yasaima.price_note: ⚠ THE URL ON THE RECORD IS DEAD. The record cites https://goryon-miyamasuzaka.owst.jp/ , which now returns HTTP 404 with an empty body — the shop's Ebica/owst page has been removed. The working source is the shop-run HotPepper card at https://www.hotpepper.jp/strJ001189400/ , and the record's website field should be repointed there. ⚠ CHECK THAT THIS SHOP IS STILL TRADING BEFORE YOU GO. Two signals sit against it: the owst page is gone, and the HotPepper card's booking widget reads 「現在ネット予約を受け付けていません」 — online reservations are switched off. The card itself was last updated 2024-05-29, so the prices below are around two years old and every one of them predates the 2025 wave of izakaya price rises. Telephone first. ⚠ SHOP FACTS from the card: open 17:00–23:30 (food and drink L.O. 22:30) seven days a week, no closing day; 65 seats including a counter and, unusually for Shibuya, TERRACE SEATING with chairs. 東京都渋谷区渋谷1-6-3 ヴィラファースト渋谷 地下1F. ⚠ WHAT THE SHOP ACTUALLY IS, AND WHY IT MATTERS FOR A VEGETARIAN. 野菜巻き串 — the Hakata speciality this shop is named for — sounds like vegetable skewers and is not. The format is a VEGETABLE WRAPPED IN PORK BELLY OR BACON and grilled: the shop's own line is 「いろんなお野菜を豚肉やベーコンで巻いちゃいましたー」. Every single one of the twenty items in the 野菜巻き串 section contains pork, bacon, cheese or egg. A vegetarian reading this section by name will order twenty skewers of meat. That is the most important thing on this record. ⚠ GLUTEN: nothing here is safe and there is no need to hunt. Skewers are finished with a soy-based tare or salt, the 炊き餃子 has a wheat wrapper, the tonkotsu ramen and champon and the 博多ラーメンサラダ are wheat noodles, 山芋の竜田揚げ and the hamukatsu are floured and fried, and 焼きそば巻き wraps a wheat noodle in pork. Even salt-only skewers pass a grill shared with tare-glazed ones. ⚠ VEGAN: effectively nothing. The only candidates are 旬なお漬けもん ¥500, ザーサイ浅漬け ¥450 and 黒糖そら豆 ¥450, all in the 呑んべい section, and each depends on seasoning the shop does not publish.

items.section: 愛され続ける【博】冷・温 一品料理
items.note: Breadcrumbed and deep fried — wheat crumb, pork.

items.ja: ムシドリとザーサイのネギサラダ
items.romaji: mushidori to zāsai no negi sarada
items.en: Steamed chicken and zhacai spring-onion salad
items.section: 愛され続ける【博】冷・温 一品料理
items.note: Chicken. The dressing is unpublished and Chinese-style ones normally carry soy sauce.

items.en: Daisen jidori liver, cooked rare, with spring-onion sauce
items.section: 愛され続ける【博】冷・温 一品料理
items.note: Chicken liver cooked at low temperature. The ネギダレ is soy-based as a rule.

items.ja: ゴルゴンハニーのチーズ豆腐
items.en: Cheese tofu with gorgonzola, honey and walnuts
items.section: 愛され続ける【博】冷・温 一品料理
items.note: Tofu in name, but the dish is dairy and honey — both animal.

items.en: Potatoes with bacon in anchovy butter
items.section: 愛され続ける【博】冷・温 一品料理
items.note: Anchovy, bacon and butter.

items.ja: 博多もつ鍋（白味噌／カレー／辛味）
items.en: Hakata offal hot pot — white miso, curry or spicy, from 2 servings
items.note: Beef offal and chicken tsukune with cabbage and garlic chives in a broth the shop says it boils from raw knuckle bones for three days and nights. Pork-bone broth, offal, miso or curry seasoning — the curry version is a wheat roux. Finishers: champon noodles ¥400 (wheat), udon ¥400 (wheat), cheese risotto ¥680 (dairy), carbonara ¥680 (wheat, dairy, egg), kuppa ¥400, spicy noodles ¥450. Refills: offal ¥650, tsukune ¥500, vegetables ¥580.

items.section: 呑んべいさんのお酒のあて
items.note: One of the only plausibly plant-based plates in the shop. Japanese pickles are usually vegetables, salt and rice bran — but many are steeped in soy sauce or a dashi brine, and the shop does not say which are on today. Ask what is in the bowl.

items.section: 呑んべいさんのお酒のあて
items.note: Zhacai is a pickled vegetable and plant-based in principle; Japanese-market packs are commonly dressed with sesame oil and sometimes chicken extract or soy. Ask.

items.section: 呑んべいさんのお酒のあて
items.note: Beans and unrefined cane sugar — the most likely genuinely vegan item on the card, and wheat-free unless the coating carries a flour dusting. Ask.

items.en: Ume-suishou — shark cartilage with pickled plum
items.section: 呑んべいさんのお酒のあて
items.note: Despite the plum in the name this is SHARK CARTILAGE. Usually dressed with soy or dashi.

items.ja: かつおのハラミの塩辛
items.section: 呑んべいさんのお酒のあて
items.note: Fermented fish.

items.section: 呑んべいさんのお酒のあて
items.note: Fish roe; the mentaiko cure normally includes soy sauce and mirin.

items.ja: クリームチーズの醤油漬
items.en: Cream cheese steeped in soy sauce
items.section: 呑んべいさんのお酒のあて
items.note: Dairy, and soy sauce is named in the dish — wheat.

items.section: 呑んべいさんのお酒のあて
items.note: Cucumber bruised and dressed. Plant-based if the dressing is — but smashed cucumber is normally dressed with sesame oil and soy sauce, which would put wheat in it. Ask for salt only.

items.ja: くらげの柚子こしょうポンズ
items.section: 呑んべいさんのお酒のあて
items.note: Jellyfish is an animal, and ponzu is soy-based.

items.section: 呑んべいさんのお酒のあて
items.note: Avocado is plant, but 漬け in an izakaya means a soy-sauce marinade — wheat, and often a dashi in the marinade too. A near-miss unless they will do it plain.

items.en: Pick any three of the above
items.section: 呑んべいさんのお酒のあて
items.note: Three small plates from this section for less than three singly. Diet answer depends entirely on which three — see the individual notes.

items.ja: 博多とんこつラーメン
items.en: Hakata tonkotsu ramen, thin noodles barikata
items.note: Pork-bone broth and thin wheat noodles.

items.en: Jidori chicken soboro and egg rice bowl
items.note: Chicken, egg and a house dashi — the soboro is simmered in soy sauce.

Rice with pickled takana — plant-based in principle and the cheapest filling thing here, but Hakata takana-zuke is normally seasoned with soy sauce and sesame oil, and is often stir-fried in lard. Ask. Toppings: mentaiko +¥150, Hakata spring onion +¥50, raw egg +¥100, all three +¥280.

items.ja: 博多明太子とキムチの皿うどん
items.note: Sara-udon uses fried wheat noodles; cod roe is fish and kimchi commonly contains salted shrimp.

items.ja: ごりょんさん【名物】パンアイス
items.en: The house bread-and-ice-cream, splits into two
items.note: Bread (wheat) and ice cream (dairy). The shop says it splits in two to share.

items.ja: はかた地どり玉子のなめらかプリン
items.en: Smooth custard pudding, Hakata jidori eggs
items.note: Egg and dairy.

items.ja: 生チョコブリュレ バニラアイス添え
items.en: Chocolate brulee with vanilla ice cream
items.note: Dairy, egg, and usually cream and chocolate containing milk.
Flavour changes daily — ask staff. Dairy unless it turns out to be a sorbet.
